transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. I'm here to help you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, doctor, I've been feeling completely emotionally numb and having these sudden, uncontrollable bursts of anger for about a month now. It's really starting to scare me, and I just don't know what to do
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, or felt so irritable or impulsive that it caused problems in your life?

I haven't felt unusually energetic or needed less sleep, but I am extremely irritable and impulsive. I am constantly on edge and will suddenly explode over trivial things, which has led to me shouting at people and even throwing objects. It's causing huge problems in my life because I just can't seem to control it.
Did these symptoms of feeling on edge and having uncontrollable outbursts begin after a specific distressing or life-threatening event?

Yes, all of these outbursts and irritability started right after a highly distressing accident I was in about a month ago. I know that event triggered all of this, but I actually can't recall the details of what happened because my memory of it is completely fragmented and blocked out.
Since that accident, do you find yourself having intrusive, unwanted thoughts or nightmares about the event, or do you actively avoid places or situations that remind you of it?

No, I haven't really experienced any nightmares or intrusive thoughts about the accident. I also haven't found myself actively trying to avoid places or things that remind me of it. It's more that my mind just feels completely blank when I try to think about that day.
Do you feel that your distress or the difficulty you are having in your daily life is significantly out of proportion to what would be expected from this accident?
I'm really not sure, and I haven't really thought about whether it's out of proportion or not. All I know is that I am struggling a lot to get through my daily life right now.
Are your current symptoms, such as the anger and emotional numbness, causing significant impairment in your social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning?
I'm not quite sure, and I haven't really thought about how much it's impairing my daily life or my work. I just know that everything feels incredibly difficult to manage right now.
Since the accident occurred one month ago, have these symptoms of emotional numbness and anger been present most of the time, or do they come and go?

They have been present consistently ever since the accident a month ago. The emotional numbness feels like a constant state of emptiness, and my nerves are always sharp and on edge rather than these feelings coming and going.
Beyond the memory loss, do you ever feel like you are detached from your own body or that the world around you feels unreal or dreamlike?

No, I don't experience anything like that. I don't feel detached from my body, and the world doesn't feel dreamlike or unreal to me. It is more that I just feel completely numb and empty on the inside.

While the symptoms emerged within one month of the event, the patient lacks the core intrusive symptoms, avoidance, and alterations in cognition/mood required for PTSD, making Adjustment Disorder the most appropriate clinical diagnosis.
